div.p: French language: change to “a poor instrument perhaps beside Italian and English” for it is richer than German, Danish or Irish.

Jesuitbred: towards the end whange change to Jesuit trained. The breeding was done in J.J.’s house and family. He thinks that the gesture against the Rector came from his carnal not from his ghostly father.

div.note: The galley proofs give this sentence as “A poor instrument, but how wonderfully they use it.” The change must have been made in page proofs, received by Budgen after 1 October (Budgen, PC to JJ 1 October 1933 (JJPL 85).
The quotation is used verbatim in JJMU 182. Budgen made a check mark in pencil, and wrote both “to be done” at the top of the sentence and “Done” over the sentence itself.

In JJMU 185 this became “The Jesuit-trained Stephen…”. The “gesture against the Rector” refers to Stephen Dedalus's protest to the head of Clongowes for the punishment he had received; as noted here, it seems to refer to JJ himself. Budgen wrote “Done" in pencil over the paragraph.

The reference is to the Right Honourable William Humble Ward, second earl of Dudley, Lord Lieutenant of Ireland, who appears in "Wandering Rocks". JJMU 123-26 mentions the man in the discussion of “Wandering Rocks”, but the specifics of JJ's suggestion are not used. The paragraph is crossed out with an “X” in pencil.
This and the following lines are written in pencil in Budgen's hand.
